A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CstNet research, constraint representation and Param20K dataset. The supplied text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison, including v4's supplementary Sections F-J. v1 has no bundled supplement; details appearing only in v4 are treated as newly documented rather than necessarily newly implemented.

before.justification: v1 reports original prism/cuboid validation, ABC constraint prediction, Parametric 20000 and MCB classification, 360 Gallery segmentation, and component ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and reports additional constraint-prediction comparisons, rotation experiments and backbone ablations. Its supplement also contains MCB classification and qualitative prediction results.

M1.justification: The two-stage architecture, constraint components, SurfaceKNN and attention mechanisms remain. However, v4 Section 3.4 and Figure 7 route intermediate constraint features through residual concatenation and max pooling into classification; v1 Section 3.5 and Figure 6 classify using the final feature, reserving the displayed skip links for segmentation. This is a limited architectural revision.

E1.justification: v4 removes 360 Gallery segmentation and MCB-B classification, while adding a rotated-Param20K test scenario and explicit constraint-prediction evaluation on Param20K. The retained supplementary MCB table corresponds to MCB-A. Parametric 20000 becoming Param20K is a rename of the same 19,739-instance, 75-class dataset; the prism/cuboid task already appears in v1.

E2.justification: v4 adds ParSeNet and HPNet as evaluated constraint-prediction comparators on ABC and Param20K, and in MCB visual comparisons. It also introduces controlled Stage 2 comparisons with PointNet, PointNet++, DGCNN and 3DGCN receiving constraints. The ordinary Param20K classification and retained MCB-A comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols test unchanged trained classifiers after rotating test clouds around +Z by 0, 45, 90, 135 and 180 degrees, and compare Stage 2 backbones using predicted versus ground-truth constraints. Figure 10 additionally reports MAD through 1 minus MSE. The general Adam configuration and 200-epoch training budget remain unchanged; newly supplied split details do not establish revised splits.

E4.justification: v4 Tables 3-4 add all-constraints-disabled controls and alternative-backbone comparisons under predicted and ground-truth constraints. Figures 9-10 add full-CstNet evaluation across prism angles and rotation robustness analysis. Individual-component and SurfaceKNN ablations remain, while v1's segmentation error examples and analysis disappear.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimation. The supplementary dataset statistics do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The Param20K classification entries change: for example, PointCNN instance accuracy changes from 61.92 to 80.25, and CstNet from 89.93 to 89.94, with its mAP changing from 92.32 to 92.72. The PDFs do not explain these revisions or establish reruns under identical settings. ABC predictor test values and MCB-A results remain unchanged, while v4 adds comparative prediction, rotation and backbone-control results and removes MCB-B and segmentation results.

T1.justification: v4 adds explicit definitions for canonicalizing axis-vector signs through the z/y/x rule in Supplement J.2 and for the plotted Acc.MAD score as 1 minus MSE. These are limited mathematical specifications; the core attention equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is provided.

C1.justification: v4 drops the highlighted segmentation-superiority claim and adds core claims about comparative constraint-prediction generalization and state-of-the-art rotation robustness. It also newly claims Param20K is the first parametric-purpose multimodal dataset. The central contributions of a constraint representation and the first constraint-aware CstNet framework remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of constraint coverage, reliance on coordinates for spherical/free-form geometry, and competitors' poorer transfer through global features. It removes v1's MCB-B domain-mismatch explanation and 360 Gallery labeling and imbalance limitations. Interpretation also strengthens without changed evidence: v1 calls the 50-degree validation gain small, whereas v4 describes significant gains from 50 to 87 degrees despite unchanged Figure 3 bars.

D1.justification: Supplement G-J newly documents prism generation and splits, the validation network and combined loss, Param20K filtering and approximately 2,200 points per cloud, MAD sign normalization, visualization processing, and iterative SurfaceKNN. These substantially expand reproducibility information for previously introduced components without establishing implementation changes. The abstract also explicitly identifies source code at the existing project page.

R1.justification: v4 introduces a dedicated parametric-point-cloud discussion and positions CstNet against primitive-fitting and segmentation approaches, adding references including SPFN, ParSeNet, HPNet and H3DNet. Added geometric-constraint and CAD-sketch literature further develops the novelty argument beyond v1's broader survey organized around input representations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten. The title, dataset and module terminology change; the separate Method Overview subsection is absorbed; and experiments are reorganized around prediction, classification and robustness. Dataset motivation and retained MCB material move into the new supplement.

P2.justification: v4 redraws the architecture, expands constraint-prediction comparison panels, adds classification and rotation plots, and supplies dataset and algorithm illustrations. The MCB table is relocated and reduced to the former A columns, while segmentation tables disappear. Figure 7 also introduces a labeling error: its B-Rep-available/lacking branches name the opposite acquisition modules from those specified in the text.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens validation through direct ParSeNet/HPNet comparisons and predicted-versus-ground-truth backbone controls, while the supplement fills substantial implementation and data-documentation gaps. These gains are offset partly by removing MCB-B results and their failure explanation while labeling the retained MCB-A table simply MCB, obscuring the boundary of the superiority claim. The reversed acquisition labels in Figure 7 also reduce clarity, limiting the net improvement.
